policy_presence.summary: Retained public Claims show scoped institutional material. Currentness and complete policy coverage remain PARTIAL.

ai_disclosure.summary: Ask the teacher how to report permitted GenAI use. Do not assume there is one disclosure format for every Lund assignment.

coursework.summary: For a compulsory assignment, check with the teacher whether GenAI is permitted and how to report it; silence in course materials is not permission.

exams.summary: For an examination, double-check teacher permission and reporting requirements. Student access to a tool does not settle the exam rules.

privacy_data_entry.summary: Student guidance prohibits uploading other students’ work, sensitive personal data or protected material, even with a student login; staff ChatGPT guidance also excludes medical information.

academic_integrity.summary: Staff and students remain responsible for their content. Passing off generated work as your own may be treated as cheating.

approved_tools.summary: Student guidance lists Copilot Chat and Gemini with student-account login. It recommends licensed tools, but staff ChatGPT/DeepL/M365 eligibility remains separate and pending.

named_ai_services.summary: Named services in retained Claims are discovery context only; eligibility and assessment permission remain unverified.

teaching_guidance.summary: Teacher guidance calls for clear course rules, learning-outcome checks and equal access; it also says students’ work must not be shared with GenAI tools.

research_guidance.summary: The policy describes GenAI as support for learning and research, not a replacement for basic skills, critical thinking or scientific method.

security_procurement.summary: Student guidance favours licensed services, but the exact Swedish procurement wording and staff-tier conditions remain unresolved here.
